note: An experiment (GAME_SPEC §13.7, Stage 54; docs/CURRICULUM.md, experiment 30) on data/benches/vapour.json: water's vapour pressure against temperature, and its heat of vaporisation from Clausius and Clapeyron's line.
title: Experiment: water's vapour pressure

steps.title: A burner under the flask
steps.text: Pick up the burner in the cabinet, then click the flask.

steps.title: Full flame, and hurry
steps.text: Right-click the burner, drag its valve fully open, then click 60x.

steps.title: Boil the air out
steps.text: Let it boil: its steam drives the air out of the flask.
steps.why: Once only water and its vapour are left in the flask, its pressure is water's vapour pressure alone.

steps.title: Off, and stoppered
steps.text: Drag the valve shut, then pick up the stopper and click the flask.

steps.title: Log its temperature
steps.text: Right-click the flask, click "+ T", open the notebook and click "5 s".

steps.title: Log its pressure
steps.text: Close the notebook, right-click the flask, click "+ kPa", open the notebook again and click "5 s".
steps.why: The gauge reads the pressure inside the sealed flask: water's vapour pressure at the flask's temperature.

steps.title: Let it cool
steps.text: Watch it cool to 45 C, its pressure falling with it.

report.label: water's heat of vaporisation
report.why: In the notebook: x the temperature as 1/K, y the pressure as ln. Clausius and Clapeyron: ln p = -dH / (R T) + c, so dH = -slope x 8.314 J/(mol K). The truth is the tables' own at 75 C (44.0 kJ/mol at 25 C, less 41.7 J/mol for each kelvin); the textbook's 40.65 is at 100 C.
